content:
If you're not in a rush to grab the latest Apple product on launch day and are willing to wait a bit, Apple's certified refurbished product store has always been a solid choice. Generally speaking, about three months or so after a new product launch, the first batch of refurbished models will appear on the official website.

Other companies have similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but note that the quality standards and warranty policies they adopt are different...

Apple Certified Refurbished Products

Buying from the Apple Certified Refurbished Store gives you roughly a 15% discount, but the products are essentially no different from brand new ones. Specifically, Apple promises to provide all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing by Apple
  • Brand new housing, completely free of any scratches or wear
  • Brand new battery, with battery life identical to new products
  • Comes with all original accessories and cables
  • Eligible for Apple's standard one-year warranty, exactly the same as new products
  • Also eligible to purchase AppleCare+ service

Basically the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box rather than the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed's pricing may be more competitive, but note that the product condition guarantees are different from Apple's:

  • Inspected and tested by the seller rather than Apple
  • Uses used housing, so there will be scratches and wear (see below)
  • Uses used battery, only guaranteed to retain at least 80% of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be original Apple products
  • Amazon provides a 90-day warranty instead of Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding scratches and wear, Amazon offers three quality tiers:

  • Premium / Excellent: No visible wear on the surface when inspected from 12 inches away
  • Good: Minor scratches, barely visible when held at arm's length from 12 inches
  • Acceptable: Scratches clearly visible and can be felt by hand

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is far more vague than Amazon about what you're getting for your money:

  • No promises whatsoever about cosmetic condition, only guarantees 'like-new performance and reliability'
  • Beyond the above, no details provided on battery condition
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier offers a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only have 90 days. The company's definitions of each tier are not clear.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want to buy something with condition and Apple warranty identical to a brand new product, the Apple Refurbished Store is clearly the top choice.

That said, Amazon Renewed's pricing can be significantly lower, so if you're willing to accept the trade-offs mentioned above, it's also a decent choice. Especially if, as we suggest, you're looking to save money by upgrading to the iPhone 17 Pro rather than this year's latest model (since the only thing you'd lose is a cable), there are indeed some pretty attractive deals:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (original price $1,599 new) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (original price $1,599 new) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (original price $1,599 new) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (original price $1,299 new) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (original price $1,299 new) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (original price $1,299 new) — Only $1 above all-time low price

As for Walmart Restored, I'd be concerned their promises are too vague, but if you're not satisfied, you can return it anytime.
